caption: Classically, velocities add like ordinary numbers in one-dimensional motion. Here the girl throws a snowball forward and then backward from a sled. The velocity of the sled relative to the Earth is v=1.0m/sv=1.0m/s size 12{ ital "v="1 "." 0`"m/s"} {}. The velocity of the snowball relative to the sled is u′u′ size 12{u rSup { size 8{'} } } {}, while its velocity relative to the Earth is uu size 12{u} {}. Classically, u=v+u′u=v+u′.

images.alt: In part a, a man is pulling a sled towards the right with a velocity v equals one point zero meters per second. A girl sitting on the sled facing forward throws a snowball toward a boy on the far right of the picture. The snowball is labeled u primed equals one point five meters per second in the direction the sled is being pulled. The boy is labelled two point five meters per second. In figure b, a similar figure is shown, but the man’s velocity is one point zero meters per second, the girl is facing backward and throwing the snowball behind the sled. The snowball is labelled u primed equals negative one point five meters per second, and the boy is labelled u equals negative zero point five meters per second.

caption: According to experiment and the second postulate of relativity, light from the car’s headlights moves away from the car at speed cc size 12{c} {} and towards the observer on the sidewalk at speed cc size 12{c} {}. Classical velocity addition is not valid.

images.alt: A car is moving towards right with velocity v. A boy standing on the side-walk observes the car. The velocity of light u primed is shown to be c as observed by the girl in the car and the velocity of light u is also c as observed by the boy.

A spacecraft is heading towards earth v equals zero point five zero zero times c. A laser beam from the ship travels towards the Earth with velocity c as shown by a vector. A second spaceship traveling away from the Earth. The velocity of the second ship and second laser are the same as the first, but in the opposite direction.

In part a, a spaceship is moving towards the earth from left to right with a velocity v equals to zero point five zero times c. In part b, the spaceship shoots the canister away from earth with same velocity. In both the cases, the velocity of the ship is v equals 0 point five zero times c toward left.
